title: Venv Module
prompt_markdown: Which built-in module creates virtual environments?

content.explanation: venv is built into the standard library.

title: Dependency File
prompt_markdown: What is the standard filename for listing pip dependencies?

title: How venv isolates packages
prompt_markdown: How does an activated virtual environment ensure that `python` and `pip` commands install packages locally rather than globally?
hints: Think about the PATH environment variable.

choices: It creates a lightweight Docker container for each process.
It prepends the virtual environment's `bin` (or `Scripts`) directory to the system `PATH` environment variable.
It compiles all Python source code to machine assembly.
It modifies the operating system kernel routing tables.
content.explanation: Activation scripts modify the shell's `PATH` variable so the virtual environment's Python and Pip executables are found before any system-wide Python installation.

title: Reproducible Dependencies
prompt_markdown: Which command is traditionally used to generate a pinned list of exact package versions currently installed in an active virtual environment?

content.explanation: `pip freeze > requirements.txt` dumps all installed packages and their exact versions (e.g. `fastapi==0.115.0`) to allow deterministic replication.

title: Lockfiles vs Loose Version Constraints
prompt_markdown: Why do modern production applications prefer lockfiles (e.g. Poetry, uv, Pipenv) over unpinned requirements files like `fastapi>=0.100`?
hints: Transient dependencies and unexpected sub-dependency upgrades breaking production.

rubric: Explains that unpinned or loosely pinned requirements can pull in broken transitive dependency updates.
Explains that lockfiles freeze the entire dependency tree deterministically with cryptographic hashes.
content.reference_answer: Loose constraints (e.g. `fastapi>=0.100`) only constrain direct dependencies; third-party transitive dependencies can update at any time and introduce breaking changes or security vulnerabilities into CI/CD builds. Lockfiles capture the exact resolved version and cryptographic hash of every direct and transitive dependency in the tree, guaranteeing 100% bit-for-bit reproducible environments across local development and cloud production.

title: Why Gitignore the Virtual Environment
prompt_markdown: Why should `.venv` directories never be committed to a Git repository?

rubric: Mentions platform-specific binary executables and C-extensions (Linux binaries fail on Windows/macOS).
Mentions repository size bloat from thousands of third-party files.
Explains that environments should be reconstructed deterministically from specification files (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml).
content.reference_answer: Virtual environments contain platform-specific binaries, symlinks, and C-extensions (e.g., compiled for Linux x86_64, which will fail on macOS ARM or Windows). In addition, committing thousands of third-party package files causes massive repository bloat. Repositories should only commit specification files (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, lockfiles) so environments can be reconstructed cleanly on any machine.
